prompt_text: Who is a reliable contractor in Joplin MO for a home remodel or repair project?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but first a couple quick questions so I can give targeted recommendations:

- What kind of work is it (full remodel, kitchen, bath, siding/roof, plumbing/electrical repair, etc.)?
- Rough budget and desired start date?
- Do you need someone for design + build or just construction/repairs?
- Any preference for small local crew vs. larger firm?

If you want immediate guidance, here are reliable ways to find and vet a contractor in Joplin plus practical next steps:

Where to look
- Ask neighbors/friends or check Nextdoor for local referrals (best for real-world recent experience).
- Google Maps and Yelp for top-rated local contractors and photos/reviews.
- Better Business Bureau (BBB) for complaints/ratings.
- Angi/HomeAdvisor and Houzz for screened pros and project galleries.
- Joplin Chamber of Commerce or local Facebook groups for reputable members.
- Check Missouri Home Builders Association or NARI (National Association of the Remodeling Industry) for certified remodelers.

How to vet candidates (quick checklist)
1. Get at least 3 written bids with the same scope and materials so you can compare apples-to-apples.
2. Verify insurance (liability + workers’ comp) and ask for copies of certificates.
3. Ask for 3 recent references and photos of finished jobs; follow up with those homeowners.
4. Confirm who will do the work (employees vs. subs) and who will supervise.
5. Check license/permits — Missouri is handled locally, so confirm the contractor will pull required Joplin permits and schedule inspections.
6. Insist on a written contract listing scope, product brands/colors, start/finish dates, payment schedule, change-order process, and warranty.
7. Use a reasonable payment schedule (e.g., small deposit, progress payments tied to milestones, hold final payment until completion and lien waivers).
8. Search the contractor’s name + “Joplin” + “complaint” or “review” to spot red flags.

Key questions to ask each contractor
- How long have you been working on projects like this?
- Can you provide local references and photos of similar completed work?
- Who will be my main point of contact on site?
- Do you carry liability insurance and workers’ comp? Can you provide certificates?
- Will you pull all necessary permits and handle inspections?
- What is your proposed start/completion schedule and payment schedule?
- How do you handle unexpected problems or change orders?
- Do you provide a written warranty?

Red flags
- No written contract or unwillingness to put details in writing
- Demands for large cash-only up-front payments
- No proof of insurance or reluctance to provide references
- Extremely low bid with pressure to accept immediately
- Poor communication or evasive answers

If you want, I can:
- Draft a short RFP / message you can send to contractors.
- Create a one-page comparison checklist to evaluate bids.
- If you share project details (scope, budget, photos), I can suggest the type/size of contractor and typical price ranges.

Tell me which of those you’d like and share the project details if you want personalized contractor names or a ready-to-send message.
